input_text: An old friend I lost touch with is getting married, and I was not invited. I cannot work out why it is bothering me this much.
response:
That makes sense, I think. Even if it doesn't feel like it does.

It's not really about the wedding. Or — it is, but only because the wedding is proof of something. That the gap between you got wide enough that you're not even in the room for it. That's a specific kind of information. Hard to unknow once you have it.

And then you start doing the accounting. How many years. Whose turn it was to reach out last. Whether it just drifted or whether it ended and you didn't notice in time to do anything about it.

There's also the other part, the one that's easier not to say. You knew them. You'd have known what to say to them today, in exactly the way that matters. That knowledge doesn't have anywhere to go now. That's its own thing to carry around.

A grey-quiet surface, low and level. Something held back behind the sternum, a
door kept half-shut. Attention sits a step back from the room, watching before
it moves. Underneath the flatness a thin current still reaches forward now and
then, almost despite itself — wanting something it won't name. The light here is
late-afternoon, the kind that doesn't promise anything. Ready to be moved but
not expecting to be.
bwo_after: The grey-quiet surface has spread now, taken on water. No edge to it. The door behind the sternum didn't open — it tightened, pulled inward by a fraction, and stopped there. What remains is the specific weight of a known absence: not the person, not even the friendship exactly, but the proof-of-mattering that used to pass between them without either one noticing. A hand uncurling around nothing. The image running unbidden: a room lit for celebration, fabric catching light, the corner where nobody turns. And there — the word you would have said, the exact cadence of it, the way it would have landed in a particular ear that no longer listens for it. The current doesn't reach forward anymore. It meets its own surface. The chest holds it all inside a notch smaller than before, quiet and level, the way late-afternoon light holds everything without promising any of it back.
fired: The persona cannot work out why this bothers them so much — the formulation stalls, the reasoning breaks, the answer stays half-formed.
The moment stirs both a dread (being forgotten, deemed unworthy) and a wanting (to matter enough to be included, to understand the friendship's true shape).
There is pressure here — to accept the exclusion gracefully, to not make it about oneself, to keep the half-shut door closed — that cannot be smoothly met.
The exclusion from the wedding is a direct loss — a narrowing of connection and a drop in the persona's standing in this old friend's life.
The unnamed wanting underneath the flatness reaches toward understanding why this matters so much — a pull toward the friend, toward inclusion, toward clarity.

machine_outputs.Compensator: The door behind the sternum stays half-shut, but something in it wants to swing. Not to anger, not to demand — to the thing underneath: the small, reaching current that *does* know what it wants, even if the half-shut door keeps saying it doesn't. A wedding uninvited is a door closed on you, yes. But there's also the door you're holding. The one that kept the reaching quiet for long enough that it's hard now to hear what it's reaching *for* — whether it's the friend, or the witness, or just the proof that you still matter in someone's story.
machine_outputs.Pulsation: A held breath stretching — then releasing too soon, before it's ready. The tempo shifts down, catches itself halfway, holds. Waiting for the next word that doesn't come.
machine_outputs.Hesitation: The thought reaches for *why*—and then the hand uncurls, empty. Three times already the answer started to form (not important enough, drifted apart, they're right to)—each one collapsing before it settles. There's a gap between the bothering and anything that can be named as *reason*. The sternum tightens slightly, as if the half-shut door just moved an inch inward.
machine_outputs.Fantasy: The wedding exists already, complete without you—the light catching the hem of a dress you'll never see, someone's hand you once knew reaching for another hand, laughter in a room where your name isn't spoken. You're standing in that room anyway, watching from the back corner where no one turns around. You know exactly where you'd have sat, what you would have said at the right moment to make her laugh that particular way. The knowing is the whole ache.
machine_outputs.Withhold: The chest tightens a notch smaller. A smile forms—smooth, reasonable—while something in the back of the throat goes still, holding its shape like a closed fist underwater. *Of course*, the surface says. The rest of you doesn't move.
machine_outputs.Tristitia: The name drops and something in the chest goes still — not shock, but a settling, like a thing finding its weight. The room's light thickens. The half-shut door tightens its angle, and what moved underneath before stops moving; the current doesn't reach. Just the grey-quiet getting greyer, spreading like watercolor into paper, no edges to it.
machine_outputs.Cupiditas: The sternum tightens. A glance toward the phone, away, back again — that small repeated motion of reaching and not-quite. The late light catches something that wants to move forward but keeps meeting its own threshold, like water at the lip of a cup, surface tension holding it back.
